title: Arts participation is a minority routine with a larger perceived local-supply base, creating a cultural access and conversion gap
source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau Household Trends and Outlook Pulse Survey, July 2026 topical tables

observations.period: July 15-August 3, 2026; arts and entertainment participation in the prior four weeks

denominator.unit: estimated U.S. civilian population age 18 and older in HTOPS Table 1; published table uses weighted population counts

live_music_dance_theater.unit: percent attending a live music, dance, or theater performance in the last four weeks

art_exhibit.unit: percent attending an art exhibit in the last four weeks

movie.unit: percent going to the movies in the last four weeks

personal_art_creation.unit: percent creating, practicing, or performing personal art in the last four weeks

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from Census HTOPS July 2026 arts Tables 1 and 2. Percentages are calculated from the published weighted counts for the total population row; the source tables define the recall windows and include a did-not-report category.
observations.uncertainty: HTOPS is an experimental data product. Weighted population counts and derived shares are not attendance frequency, spending, access quality, artistic intensity, or causal effects. The four-week window and nonresponse category limit comparisons with annual participation surveys.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults age 18 and older; the tables provide age, sex, race and ethnicity, education, income, disability, and other select-characteristic rows.
observations.counterinterpretation: A low recent attendance share does not mean cultural disengagement: people may create art, participate outside the four-week window, use digital or informal cultural routes, or face supply, cost, time, transportation, or preference constraints.

observations.period: July 15-August 3, 2026; perceived neighborhood or community arts supply

denominator.unit: estimated U.S. civilian population age 18 and older in HTOPS Table 3; published table uses weighted population counts

plenty_of_local_opportunities.unit: percent agreeing or strongly agreeing that there are plenty of opportunities to take part in arts and cultural activities in their neighborhood or community

strongly_agree_local_opportunities.unit: percent strongly agreeing that there are plenty of local arts and cultural opportunities

disagree_or_strongly_disagree_local_oppo.unit: percent disagreeing or strongly disagreeing that there are plenty of local arts and cultural opportunities

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from Census HTOPS July 2026 arts Table 3; agreement and disagreement shares are calculated from the published weighted counts and retain did-not-report responses outside the displayed combined categories.
observations.uncertainty: Perceived local supply is not an inventory of venues, affordability, accessibility, transportation, or program quality. The difference between perceived supply and recent participation is a descriptive gap, not evidence that supply causes attendance.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults age 18 and older; published rows include select demographic and socioeconomic characteristics.
observations.counterinterpretation: People can perceive adequate cultural supply while not attending because of price, time, caregiving, health, transportation, preferences, or the four-week recall window; conversely, attendance can occur despite a weak local supply perception through travel or digital routes.

boundary: This record adds a current cultural-participation and perceived-local-supply layer. It does not measure cultural spending, venue capacity, artistic quality, durable engagement, identity, wellbeing, or causal access barriers, and the calculated shares should not be treated as respondent-level longitudinal outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Census HTOPS July 2026 publication page and arts XLS tables retrieved; total-row counts, recall windows, weighted-population framing, agreement categories, and experimental-data warning cross-checked against the publication.
